title: Permea Metrics Specification
description: Which metrics a benchmark reports, which one is primary, and -- critically -- each metric's chance reference. The chance_reference abstraction is the extensibility hook that lets regression be added in 1.1 without a breaking change (amendment A3).

task_type.$comment: Must agree with label_schema.task_type. Cross-document consistency is checked by the validator, not by the schema.

primary.$comment: PR-AUC, not ROC-AUC, is the recommended default under class imbalance. ROC-AUC is optimistic and stable-looking when negatives vastly outnumber positives -- exactly the regime these benchmarks live in (B3Pred Dataset_3 is 269 pos / 2690 neg). We do not FORBID roc_auc as primary; we make the choice visible.

chance_reference.$comment: EXTENSIBILITY HOOK. Paper 1's harness hardcoded `0.5 if metric == roc_auc else base_rate`, which is a binary-classification assumption baked into the inference layer. Declaring the chance reference per metric instead means a regression task (chance R^2 = 0) slots in additively, with no change to the bootstrap or permutation code. This is the single change that keeps mRNA expression from forcing a 2.0.

enrichment.description: Optional top-k% enrichment reporting (precision at top-k divided by base rate). Useful because it is the metric a screening campaign actually cares about, and it can stay meaningful when PR-AUC collapses.

allOf.$comment: Task dispatch. Adding regression = adding a branch here plus a regression_metric $def. Existing documents remain valid.

$reserved_regression_metric.$comment: NOT ACTIVE IN 1.0. Documented to show the extension is additive and to fix the vocabulary before anyone else does. Activating it in 1.1 requires: widen task_type enum, add an allOf branch, add chance_reference defaults (r2: 0, spearman: 0, rmse: 'empirical_permutation'). No existing document breaks.
